tldr: Rod Johnson presents Embabel, a JVM agent framework on Spring AI that uses a deterministic GOAP planner instead of an LLM to choose the next action.
summary: Rod Johnson introduces Embabel, a JVM-native agent framework built on Spring AI and Spring Boot. It takes the opposite approach to frameworks that ask a language model to decide what to do next, which can leave non-reproducible traces that are hard to explain.

Its core is Goal-Oriented Action Planning (GOAP), borrowed from game AI: developers declare goals and annotate actions with @Action and @AchievesGoal, and a deterministic non-LLM planner chains them by pre- and post-conditions. The plan is inspectable before it runs and explainable afterwards. The listing notes that full session details were still pending.
keyPoints: Embabel is built on Spring AI and Spring Boot.
Planning uses GOAP, a deterministic algorithm rather than an LLM.
Plans can be inspected before execution and explained after.
takeaways: Consider deterministic planning where you need reproducible, explainable agent behaviour.
watchIf: You build agents on the JVM and need reproducible, explainable behaviour.
